Allele frequencies and marker summaries

Source: R/AllGenerics.R, R/accessors.R
alleleFrequency.Rd

Computes, for every marker, the frequency of the counted allele, the minor allele frequency, the call rate and the observed heterozygosity.

Usage

alleleFrequency(x, ...)

# S4 method for class 'BreedingExperiment'
alleleFrequency(x, tol = 1e-08, ...)

Arguments

x

A BreedingExperiment object.

...

Unused.

tol

How far a dosage may sit from a whole number and still count as a genotype call when heterozygosity is computed.

Value

A S4Vectors::DataFrame with one row per marker and columns freq, maf, callRate and heterozygosity.

Details

freq and maf use every dosage that is present, so an expected dosage from imputation contributes to them on the same footing as a call. callRate is the proportion of dosages that are not NA; after imputeMarkers() that is 1 for every marker, so take call rates before imputing if you need them.

heterozygosity is different, because a heterozygote is a genotype rather than a quantity. A cell counts towards it only if it is a genotype call: its dosage must be a whole number, and it must not be marked in the imputed assay that imputeMarkers() writes. Everything else is left out of both the numerator and the denominator. Without those two checks an imputed cell would be counted as a non-heterozygote and heterozygosity would appear to fall every time a data set was imputed. A marker with no genotype call at all gets NA.

Dosages imputed by other software arrive without the imputed assay, so only the whole-number check applies to them; pass such dosages in as fractional values, or carry your own mask as an extra assay, if observed heterozygosity matters to you.

See also

filterMarkers(), imputeMarkers()

Examples

set.seed(1)
be <- simulateBreeding(n_ind = 30, n_marker = 50)
head(alleleFrequency(be))
#> DataFrame with 6 rows and 4 columns
#>              freq       maf  callRate heterozygosity
#>         <numeric> <numeric> <numeric>      <numeric>
#> snp0001  0.450000  0.450000         1       0.633333
#> snp0002  0.333333  0.333333         1       0.466667
#> snp0003  0.500000  0.500000         1       0.600000
#> snp0004  0.816667  0.183333         1       0.233333
#> snp0005  0.333333  0.333333         1       0.333333
#> snp0006  0.800000  0.200000         1       0.266667

# imputation does not change the observed heterozygosity of a marker,
# because imputed cells are not counted as genotype calls
bem <- simulateBreeding(n_ind = 30, n_marker = 50, missing = 0.2)
all.equal(alleleFrequency(bem)$heterozygosity,
          alleleFrequency(imputeMarkers(bem))$heterozygosity)
#> [1] TRUE
